summary.title: Tutorial series: learning how to write a 3D soft engine from scratch in C#, TypeScript or JavaScript
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a CPU-only "soft engine" that projects and rotates a cube's vertices on screen, covering camera, mesh, and device objects with matrix transforms.
takeaways: A 3D scene is drawn each frame by transforming vertices through world, view and projection matrices (worldMatrix * viewMatrix * projectionMatrix).
A back buffer is a pixel array written by PutPixel and then flushed to the screen; the canvas getImageData/putImageData approach is used in HTML5.
Vertices are projected from 3D to 2D screen coordinates, with clipping before drawing points.
Rotation should be applied before translation when building the world matrix.
The series progresses from points to wireframe, rasterization with Z-buffer, flat and Gouraud shading, and textures.
summary.summary: The article introduces a six-part (plus bonus) tutorial series on writing a software 3D renderer that uses only the CPU, with code in C#, TypeScript and JavaScript. Part 1 covers the core: Camera and Mesh classes, a cube defined by 8 vertices, and a Device object that builds view and projection matrices, applies world transforms, projects vertices to 2D, and draws them as pixels in a back buffer. The author recommends reading matrix background resources first and treats matrix math as a black box, using SharpDX or babylon.math libraries. Written for Visual Studio 2012 and TypeScript 0.9, so the code targets old toolchains.
